$$0 \to \mathcal{I}_{L \cup M \cup N}(3) \to \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^4}(3) \to \mathcal{O}_{L \cup M \cup N}(3) \to 0.$$

Two general $\mathbb{P}^2$'s in $\mathbb{P}^4$ meet in a point ($\dim L + \dim M = 4 = \dim \mathbb{P}^4$), and three general $\mathbb{P}^2$'s have empty triple intersection ($2+2+2 = 6 > 4$). Using the Mayer–Vietoris exact sequence for unions:
$$0 \to \mathcal{O}_{L \cup M}(3) \to \mathcal{O}_L(3) \oplus \mathcal{O}_M(3) \to \mathcal{O}_{L \cap M}(3) \to 0,$$
so $h^0(\mathcal{O}_{L \cup M}(3)) = 10 + 10 - 1 = 19$. Then:
$$0 \to \mathcal{O}_{L \cup M \cup N}(3) \to \mathcal{O}_{L \cup M}(3) \oplus \mathcal{O}_N(3) \to \mathcal{O}_{(L \cup M) \cap N}(3) \to 0,$$
where $(L \cup M) \cap N = \{p_{LN}\} \cup \{p_{MN}\}$ (two distinct points), giving $h^0(\mathcal{O}_{(L\cup M)\cap N}) = 2$. Thus:
$$h^0(\mathcal{O}_{L \cup M \cup N}(3)) = 19 + 10 - 2 = 27.$$

The restriction map $H^0(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^4}(3)) \to H^0(\mathcal{O}_{L \cup M \cup N}(3))$ is surjective: this follows inductively from the surjectivity of restriction to each $\mathbb{P}^2$ (standard for linear subspaces) and the transversality of intersections. Hence $H^1(\mathcal{I}_{L \cup M \cup N}(3)) = 0$, and:
$$h^0(\mathcal{I}_{L \cup M \cup N}(3)) = 35 - 27 = 8.$$

**Step 2: Six additional general point conditions.**

Let $Z = \{q_1, \dots, q_6\}$ be six general points in $\mathbb{P}^4$. From the exact sequence
$$0 \to \mathcal{I}_{L \cup M \cup N \cup Z}(3) \to \mathcal{I}_{L \cup M \cup N}(3) \xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}} \mathcal{O}_Z \to 0,$$
we need the evaluation map $\mathrm{ev}: H^0(\mathcal{I}_{L \cup M \cup N}(3)) \to \mathbb{C}^6$ to be surjective.

The base locus of the linear system $|\mathcal{I}_{L \cup M \cup N}(3)|$ is exactly $L \cup M \cup N$: the ideal $I_{L \cup M \cup N} = I_L \cap I_M \cap I_N$ is generated in degrees $\leq 3$ (each $I_{\Lambda_i}$ is generated by linear forms, and the intersection of ideals generated in degree 1 is generated in degree $\leq 3$), so the degree-3 part generates the full ideal, whose vanishing set is $L \cup M \cup N$.

For any point $q \notin L \cup M \cup N$, evaluation at $q$ is a nonzero linear functional on the 8-dimensional space $H^0(\mathcal{I}_{L \cup M \cup N}(3))$. Six general points give six linear functionals in general position on an 8-dimensional space (since $6 \leq 8$ and the functionals vary over a non-degenerate family), so they are linearly independent. The evaluation map is surjective, giving:
$$h^0(\mathcal{I}_{L \cup M \cup N \cup Z}(3)) = 8 - 6 = 2.$$

**Conclusion.** The dimension of the space of cubic polynomials in $\mathbb{P}^4$ vanishing on three general codimension-2 subspaces and at six general points is:

$$\boxed{2}$$
